scoringCalibration: Two eye-quality points are restored because the previous flat iris, uniform sclera vessels, painted upper-fold strips and duplicate limbal geometry are replaced by a deterministic owned texture set, body-integrated palpebral rolls and a deeper collision-cleared corneal envelope. The strict score remains low because the eyelid aperture topology, facial identity, skin microstructure, crown groom, clothing and deformation system are still below production quality.
visualFindings: The iris now contains layered green-hazel fibers, an irregular collarette, crypt breakup and a texture-integrated limbal fade instead of bright straight overlay spokes.
Scleral vessels now branch from the corners over a warm nonuniform base instead of repeating as parallel horizontal lines across the whole eye.
Upper and lower palpebral rolls are sculpted into the body surface with canthus taper and a 0.639 mm maximum displacement; the detached painted upper-fold strips are excluded from render and runtime.
The corneal anterior envelope gains a 1.55 mm central bulge, with tear film, caruncle and lash roots reprojected against both body and cornea clearances.
Fixed front, both three-quarter and full-face views no longer show the rejected floating limbal black arc or the previous red upper-fold outline.
rejectedExperiments: v58 regional vertex-color and skin-shader amplification was rejected because fixed-camera comparisons produced too little visible facial improvement.
v59 detached eyelid margins were rejected because they repeated the floating-patch architecture of v48 and introduced lower-lid collisions at neutral and posed frames.
v60 body-only palpebral rolls were retained as architectural evidence but rejected as a release candidate because the close-view improvement was too small without rebuilding the eye shading stack.
The first v61 limbal placement was rejected after three-quarter renders exposed a detached black arc; the redundant mesh is now runtime-excluded and its darkening is integrated into the iris texture.
blockingFailures: The face still lacks production expression loops, asymmetric commissure structure and verified phoneme deformation.
The current body-integrated lid roll improves thickness but the eye aperture remains constrained by legacy topology and cannot yet blink or squint with anatomical fold behavior.
Skin still lacks production pore, peach-fuzz, oil-zone and regionally calibrated subsurface response under multiple lighting environments.
The extreme top view still exposes a radial hair-ribbon fan; the side curtain and rear split remain visible.
Clothing edge flow, seams, folds, fabric materials and outer-layer combinations remain below review quality.
Raised-arm shoulders still require corrective deformation and the standard pose suite remains incomplete.
Signed clothing-distance samples remain negative despite zero exact triangle overlaps in the audited frames.
Actual browser GPU frame time, memory and LOD transition popping for v61 remain unmeasured because the accepted website preview has deliberately not been replaced.
